title: Bitin'
primary_topics: The Senate impeachment court recessing on March 22 before the defense could explain the most damning prosecution evidence -- the peso deposits and undisclosed dollar accounts
Two pending SC cases that could be game-changers during the six-week recess: the PSBank TRO petition and Corona petition to nullify the entire Senate proceedings
The many unanswered questions Corona must resolve during the recess -- SALN corrections, dollar account disclosure, witness stand decision -- that will shape the trial course
sub_topics: 34 days of trial spanning nearly three months; adjourned March 22 before defense finished on SALN inadequacies and inconsistencies
Most significant unanswered: dollar accounts -- PSBank president Garcia admitted five foreign currency deposits belonging to Corona; sums not yet disclosed

First SC case: PSBank petition to bar public disclosure of dollar deposits; SC already issued TRO; if SC lifts TRO, defense burden becomes more stringent
Senate March 12 order: prosecution deemed to have rested case, subject to reservation on dollar account evidence pending SC ruling

SC did not issue TRO on the Senate proceedings case (unlike the PSBank case)

Pulse Asia survey: 47% believe guilty; 5% innocent; 43% undecided; 60% do not trust; 11% trust; 29% undecided
Defense strong in legalities but failed to win the people -- 6-week recess gives breathing space to revise PR strategy

stances.claim: The trial adjourned short of expectations -- bitin -- because the defense has not yet explained the most damning prosecution evidence: the peso deposits and the admitted but undisclosed dollar accounts.
stances.rhetorical_move: bitin-as-analytical-verdict on the incomplete state of the trial

stances.claim: The two pending SC cases are potentially decisive game-changers: if the SC allows inquiry into dollar accounts, the defense burden becomes more stringent; if the SC voids the Senate proceedings, the entire trial becomes obsolete -- though the OSG argues the Senate acted prudently within its constitutional bounds.
stances.rhetorical_move: two-game-changer-SC-cases analysis identifying the most consequential pending decisions

stances.claim: Corona faces six crucial self-determining decisions during the recess: SALN declarations, peso and dollar account disclosures, real estate admissions, and SALN corrections -- with the painful irony that corrections could constitute admissions of guilt rather than exonerations.

notable_anecdotes: The Pulse Asia survey showing 60% of Filipinos do not trust Corona while only 11% do -- and 47% believe him guilty vs only 5% innocent -- establishing that despite the defense legal strength in technicalities, it has catastrophically lost the Court of Public Opinion.

The ironic SALN correction dilemma: if Corona corrects his previous SALNs to disclose omitted assets, the corrections could be deemed admissions of guilt rather than exonerations -- the perfect legal trap of his own making.

The 6-week recess framed by CJ as giving the defense breathing space to revise its public relations strategy -- implicitly observing that legal skill without public trust is insufficient in an impeachment trial that is more political than legal.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban reports that after 34 days of trial spanning nearly three months, the Senate impeachment court recessed on March 22 -- leaving the defense short of having explained the most damning prosecution evidence: the peso deposits and the undisclosed sums in the five PSBank dollar accounts admitted by PSBank president Pascual Garcia III. He describes the trial's suspended state as 'bitin.' During the six-week recess (resuming May 7), two pending SC cases could prove decisive: the PSBank petition to bar disclosure of the dollar deposits (SC has already issued a TRO; if lifted, the defense burden becomes more stringent); and Corona's petitions (February 8 and 13) to nullify the entire impeachment complaint and Senate proceedings (SC did not issue a TRO; the OSG argues the Senate acted within its constitutional bounds). The Pulse Asia survey shows 47% believe Corona guilty, 60% distrust him -- the defense has failed to win the people, giving it breathing space to revise its public relations strategy. Corona faces six crucial recess decisions: disclose acquisition cost or market values in his new SALN; disclose actual peso and dollar account sums; admit owning more than five real estate assets; correct previous SALNs; and face the painful paradox that SALN corrections could constitute admissions of guilt. Bitin!
